subject: Maths
subtopic: Equations with unknowns on both sides
title: Equations with unknowns on both sides
subtitle: Solving Linear Equations · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can solve linear equations where the unknown appears on both sides.

key_vocab.definition: When x appears on both sides of the equation, collect all x terms on one side and all number terms on the other by using inverse operations.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can solve linear equations where the unknown appears on both sides.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: x appears on both sides -- When x appears on both sides of the equation, collect all x terms on one side and all number terms on the other by using inverse operations.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Collect x terms on one side, number terms on the other, then solve.
5x + 3 = 2x + 12 ⇒ 3x = 9 ⇒ x = 3
Subtract 2x from both sides, then subtract 3 from both sides

Key examples:
  ✓ 5x + 3 = 2x + 12: subtract 2x, get 3x + 3 = 12, x = 3  (collect x terms)
  ✓ 7x − 4 = 3x + 8: subtract 3x, get 4x − 4 = 8, x = 3  (move smaller x)
  ✓ Always move the smaller x coefficient to keep x positive  (good practice)
  ✗ 5x + 3 = 2x + 12 gives 7x = 15  (cannot add x terms across =)
  ✗ 5x + 3 = 2x + 12 gives 3x = 15 directly  (forgot to subtract 3 from both sides)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – x terms positive
  Solve 5x + 2 = 3x + 10
  Subtract 3x: 2x + 2 = 10
  Subtract 2: 2x = 8
  Divide by 2: x = 4
  x = 4
  (Move the smaller x term (3x) to get a positive coefficient.)

Example 2 – larger coefficient on right
  Solve 2x + 9 = 5x − 3
  Subtract 2x: 9 = 3x − 3
  Add 3: 12 = 3x
  Divide by 3: x = 4
  x = 4
  (Move 2x to keep x positive on the right.)

sections.title: Larger coefficient on right
sections.content:
Move x to the side with the larger coefficient.

(a) 2x + 10 = 5x + 1
(b) x + 9 = 4x
(c) 3x + 1 = 7x − 11
(d) x + 14 = 3x + 2

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ 5x + 3 = 2x + 12 becomes 3x + 3 = 12 (subtract 2x from both sides)
✗ 5x + 3 = 2x + 12 becomes 7x + 3 = 12
✓ Move the smaller x term to avoid negative coefficients
✗ You can add x terms from different sides: 5x + 2x = 7x
✓ After collecting terms, solve as a one-step or two-step equation

teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Simple equations:
  (a) x = 3
  (b) x = 4
  (c) x = 3
  (d) x = 4

Larger coefficient on right:
  (a) x = 3
  (b) x = 3
  (c) x = 3
  (d) x = 6

With negatives:
  (a) x = 4
  (b) x = 3
  (c) x = 3
  (d) x = 3

With brackets:
  (a) x = 3
  (b) x = 3
  (c) x = 2
  (d) x = 4

Mixed problems:
  (a) x = 3
  (b) x = 6
  (c) x = 5
  (d) x = 2
  (e) x = 4
